cards.text: Naomi is back in Bethlehem with her daughter-in-law Ruth, a woman from Moab, and the barley harvest is just starting. Now here's a name to hold onto, friend: Boaz. He's a relative on Naomi's husband's side, a prominent man of noble character from the clan of Elimelech.

cards.question: Ruth comes to Naomi with a plan. What does she ask Naomi to let her do?

answers.text: Go glean grain in the fields
Find work in the town market
Go back home to Moab

cards.question: Naomi hears Ruth's plan and tells her to stay home instead. True or false?

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: So Ruth heads out and gleans after the harvesters. The text says she "happened" to come to a certain part of the field, and friend, I LOVE it when the Bible says something just happened.

cards.question: Whose part of the field does Ruth happen to come to?

answers.text: Boaz
Gideon
Nabal

cards.text: Just then Boaz arrives from Bethlehem and says to the harvesters, "The LORD be with you." Friend, at most jobs the boss walks in and everybody gets SUPER interested in their screen, but not here. "The LORD bless you," the harvesters reply.

cards.question: Boaz spots someone new in his field and walks right up to ask her who she is. True or false?

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: The foreman answers, "She is the Moabitess who returned with Naomi from the land of Moab." He says she asked to glean and gather among the sheaves after the harvesters.

cards.question: The foreman has one more thing to report about Ruth. How long has she been working?

answers.text: Since morning with one short rest
Only since the middle of the day
Just a few minutes so far

cards.text: Morning until now with one short rest, and friend, I have taken longer breaks than that deciding between sprinkles and mango bits. Then Boaz turns to Ruth himself: "Listen, my daughter."

cards.question: Boaz tells Ruth not to glean in another ___ and to stay close to his servant girls.

answers.text: field
town
village

cards.question: Boaz tells Ruth he has ordered the young men not to touch her. True or false?

answers.text: True
False

cards.question: Boaz thinks of one more thing for Ruth. What can she do when she gets thirsty?

answers.text: Drink from the jars the young men filled
Walk back into town for a drink
Draw water from the well herself

cards.text: At this, Ruth falls on her face, bowing low to the ground. I bet she did not see ANY of this coming when she walked out the door this morning.

cards.question: Bowing low before Boaz, Ruth asks him a question. What is it?

answers.text: Why he would take notice of a foreigner
Whether Naomi can glean here too
What she owes him for the water

cards.question: Boaz answers Ruth. He says he has been made fully aware of all she has done for her ___ since her husband died.

answers.text: mother-in-law
sister-in-law
father

cards.text: He knows she left her father and mother and the land of her birth, and came to a people she did not know before. Then Boaz wishes her a rich reward for her work, and he says she has taken refuge under someone's wings.

cards.question: Boaz says Ruth has taken refuge under someone's wings. Whose wings are they?

answers.text: The God of Israel
The clan of Elimelech
The elders of Bethlehem

cards.text: Ruth tells him she hopes to keep finding favor in his eyes, for he has comforted her and spoken kindly to her. And she points out she is not even like one of his servant girls.
At mealtime, Boaz calls Ruth over: "Come over here; have some bread and dip it into the vinegar sauce." She sits down beside the harvesters, and Boaz offers her roasted grain.

cards.question: Boaz offers Ruth roasted grain at mealtime. How does her meal turn out?

answers.text: She is satisfied with some left over
She only gets a few quick bites
She skips it to keep on gleaning

cards.text: When Ruth gets up to glean again, Boaz gives his young men some orders. Friend, when the boss pulls the whole crew aside like that, EVERYBODY on that crew starts wondering who's in trouble.

cards.question: Boaz tells his young men they may insult Ruth if she gathers among the sheaves. True or false?

answers.text: True
False

cards.question: Boaz goes even further. What does he tell the young men to do for Ruth?

answers.text: Pull out stalks from the bundles for her
Carry all of her grain into town
Give her a share of their own wages

cards.text: So Ruth gathers grain in the field until evening, then beats out what she gleaned. Me, I spent years in the back of a junk drawer, and the only thing I ever gathered was DUST.

cards.question: When Ruth beats out her grain, it comes to about an ephah of ___.

answers.text: barley
spelt
millet

cards.text: She picks up the grain and carries it into town, where Naomi sees what she gleaned. I bet Naomi's jaw hit the floor.

cards.question: Ruth brings out something else for Naomi besides the grain. What is it?

answers.text: What she saved from her meal
A gift of silver from Boaz
A water jar from the field

cards.text: Naomi has questions: "Where did you glean today, and where did you work?" Friend, I bet that's somebody who wants the WHOLE story, and she wants it NOW.

cards.question: Naomi blesses the man who noticed Ruth before Ruth even tells her his name. True or false?

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: Ruth tells her the name of the man she worked with: Boaz. And Naomi says, "May he be blessed by the LORD, who has not withdrawn His kindness from the living or the dead."

cards.question: Naomi keeps going. What does she tell Ruth about Boaz?

answers.text: He is one of their kinsman-redeemers
He is a priest at the tabernacle
He is a judge over all Israel

cards.text: Then Ruth tells Naomi something else Boaz told her. Oh, friend, it gets BETTER.

cards.question: How long does Ruth say Boaz told her to stay with his young men?

answers.text: Until they finish gathering all his harvest
Until the end of this one week
Until the next Sabbath day comes

cards.question: Naomi says it is good for Ruth to work with Boaz's young women. Why?

answers.text: So nothing will happen to her in another field
So Boaz will pay her a fair wage
So she can learn the customs of Israel

cards.question: Ruth stays close to Boaz's servant girls only until the barley harvest is finished. True or false?

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: And all that time, Ruth lives with her mother-in-law. That's where we'll set this batch on the rack for now, friend, because this story is just getting warmed up.

findings.problem: This non-opening story card has three sentences: Boaz's greeting, the workplace joke, and the harvesters' reply.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The actual endpoint in Ruth 2:23 is never stated. Card 17 only establishes that staying only until the barley harvest is false, and this card's 'all that time' does not explain that Ruth gleans until both the barley and wheat harvests are finished.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.
